answer_1.quote: Zero Pronoun Translation When pronouns are omitted in a source sentence, ZPT aims to generate ZPs in its target translation.
answer_1.outputs: English translations of Chinese source sentences, with recovered zero pronouns

answer_2.quote: We used case-insensitive tokenBLEU to measure the overall translation quality... To measure the performance of ZPT, we used a variant of APT... We also report correlation with METEOR and COMET.

answer_4.quote: For human evaluation, we randomly select a hundred groups of samples from each domain... we asked expert raters to score all of these samples in 1 to 5 scores to reflect the quality of ZP translations.
answer_4.guideline: Evaluation protocol based on five error categories: (1) semantics loss due to ZP anaphora misunderstanding, (2) semantics preserved but ZP errors, (3) grammatical errors due to missing ZPs, (4) ZP incorrectly translated or omitted but meaning retained, (5) meaning and all ZPs correctly translated.
